qs.q: A 62-year-old man with intermediate-risk localised prostate cancer is planned for external beam radiotherapy. How long is concurrent androgen deprivation therapy typically administered alongside radiotherapy in this risk group?
qs.e: For intermediate-risk prostate cancer treated with external beam radiotherapy, concurrent androgen deprivation therapy is given for 4 to 6 months. High-risk disease requires a longer duration of 2 to 3 years.
qs.s: Prostate Cancer: Screening, Diagnosis, Staging and Treatment: MCQs

qs.q: A patient with an upper-third squamous cell carcinoma receives external beam radiotherapy for palliation of dysphagia. What temporary side effect might the patient experience shortly after starting treatment?
o: Spontaneous healing of any pre-existing tracheo-oesophageal fistula
Immediate total obstruction secondary to massive tumour swelling
Permanent cessation of all salivary secretions
Briefly worsening dysphagia due to radiation oesophagitis
qs.e: Radiotherapy is good for pain and dysphagia, particularly for upper third SCC, but oesophagitis can briefly worsen dysphagia. Radiotherapy combined with a stent also raises the risk of bleeding and perforation.
qs.s: Oesophageal Cancer: Dysphagia, Staging, Oesophagectomy and Palliation: MCQs
